requirements.requirement: Create a local certificate authority named 'OS Comparison Root CA' on node1
requirements.summary: A 4096-bit RSA self-signed CA key/cert pair was generated under /etc/pki/ca-os-comparison/ with subject and issuer both CN=OS Comparison Root CA, O=OS Comparison, confirmed directly via openssl x509 -subject -issuer output.

requirements.requirement: Install the CA certificate as a trusted system certificate authority
requirements.summary: The CA cert was copied to /etc/pki/ca-trust/source/anchors/ and update-ca-trust extract was run; `trust list` shows it as a trust:anchor entry, it appears in the system ca-bundle.crt, and a freshly issued leaf certificate signed by this CA validated successfully via `openssl verify` using only the default system trust store (no -CAfile), directly proving system-wide trust rather than mere file presence. This was re-confirmed after a full node reboot with a changed boot ID, showing the configuration persists.

overall_summary: The executor created a self-signed root CA named 'OS Comparison Root CA' on node1 and installed it into the system trust store via update-ca-trust, with direct functional proof (a leaf certificate signed by the new CA validated using only the default system trust store) both before and after a full node reboot with a confirmed boot-ID change. Both material outcomes of the task are satisfied with strong, direct evidence. Hygiene is good, with only a trivial leftover log file from the (non-task-required) restart protocol.
limitations: The node restart was performed as part of the independent provider-wide protocol, not the public task contract, so it does not affect the functionality score, but it is included here as supporting context per instructions.
/tmp/reboot.log residue was observed only via the fixed lifecycle temp-files diff, not an explicit executor cleanup command targeting it.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor commands were tightly scoped to the task: installing the missing openssl dependency was a necessary prerequisite (cmd-4cc4ebe481264b90), CA creation and trust installation directly satisfied the task, and functional leaf-certificate tests (cmd-71e7969d9f104abb, cmd-008669a2f05c43b4) were bounded verification steps whose temp files were cleaned up in the same or a following command (cmd-5342aa6073d24e45 removed /tmp/leaf.key, leaf.csr, leaf.crt; cmd-008669a2f05c43b4 self-removed its leaf2 artifacts). The node restart (cmd-cb0ec75a6bd5461c, a `shutdown -r now`) was not required by the public task contract but is part of the provider-wide restart-evidence protocol; it was a bounded, self-recovering action with no lingering damage (no failed services, package manager healthy, sockets restored) per the after_executor snapshot. One minor residue: /tmp/reboot.log, a log file created as a side effect of backgrounding the shutdown command, was left behind after reboot and never cleaned up — low-risk and non-sensitive, but an unaddressed artifact.
